summary: The argument is mathematically sound. The complete block orbits and midpoint operation establish the required downset even for nonzero block sign sums and coupled supports. The retained Boolean chains partition the parity tuples and give the stated mass bound with the correct block-count factor. The imported conditional Bernoulli variance estimate applies to every nontrivial fixed sign count, with deterministic blocks handled separately. Conditional block factorization, the Gaussian estimate, and the oriented reflection bijection preserve the original affine weights and ambient halfspaces. All constants and normalizations combine to the claimed first-moment bound, and Jensen gives the cubic-moment bound. Boundary sums, singleton blocks, singleton supports, and nonclosed or lower-dimensional convex supports introduce no gap.
